brief.headline: You're 1.36% of their sales — use that to squeeze faster payment for a small price cut, and line up Gulshan or Tirupati as a second source.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for ₹63–64/KG, a 4–5% cut from today's ₹66.48/KG.
priceAsk.basis: The open market for Anhydrous Dextrose IP sits at ₹60–81/kg, typically ₹66–73/kg — our ₹66.48/KG is fair but sits at the upper end of typical. A move to ₹63–64 puts us safely mid-market and still gives them margin (they keep 2.3% profit). Frame it as 'we want mid-market, not top-of-band'.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay on delivery (0 days) in exchange for the price cut — cash now is worth real money to a company that owes 2.25x what it owns.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Shifting from 30 days to 0 days frees up ₹1.24 Cr of our cash that's sitting with them — we give that back only if they give us the price.

brief.financialLeverage: They owe ₹238.85 Cr — 2.25 times their own cash — so they need money coming in fast. They keep only 2.3% of every ₹100 they sell, so there's not much profit cushion, but your ₹15.03 Cr is 1.36% of their ₹1102.11 Cr in sales — losing you would sting. Their health score is D (21/100), meaning tight finances but not collapse. Push confidently on terms and a modest price cut, but don't squeeze so hard you destabilise supply — you need steady dextrose. Offer faster payment as the carrot, and quietly qualify a second source as the stick.

evidence.point: We're 1.36% of everything they sell — real leverage.
They owe more than twice what they own — cash is tight for them.
They keep only a sliver of profit — squeeze gently.
Our price sits at the top of the typical market band.
Paying them 30 days late costs us ₹1.24 Cr tied up — we can trade that for price.
evidence.figure: ₹1.24 Cr working capital freed if we move to 0 days

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch and polyol maker, ₹2359.06 Cr revenue, health score B (62/100) — a much stronger, drop-in alternate to Sayaji for dextrose; qualify them to create real competition.

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore maize wet-miller, makes Dextrose ANHYDROUS (exact form), ₹365.39 Cr revenue — confirm IP monograph CoA, then a credible second source.

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist, ₹821.13 Cr revenue, health C (53/100) — growing dextrose capacity, worth an RFQ.

risks: They're in weak financial shape (D score, 2.25x debt) — if we push too hard on price and they can't deliver, our production stops. Keep the ask modest and have a backup ready.

We already pay ₹66.48/KG, the best price we pay anyone — so we have no internal benchmark lower than this. Justify the cut purely on the market band (₹60–81, typical ₹66–73) and on the value of faster payment to them.
Their profit margin is only 2.3% — a 4–5% price cut eats into that. If they refuse, be ready to split the difference or take a smaller cut (₹65/KG) in exchange for 15-day payment instead of 0.
The open-market export figure is ₹0.00/kg — that data point is broken, so don't rely on it. Lean on the market-ask band (₹60–81/kg) and the alternates instead.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: You're a key dextrose partner for us — ₹15 crore a year — and we'd like to keep it that way, but we need you at mid-market price and we're ready to pay you faster to get there.
